title: Qualican
summary: Qualican is recorded as a locality on Mastic Neck in Brookhaven. The name appears in the 1700 William Smith deed connected with lands for the Unkechaug people at Pusspatok.
history_content: Qualican belongs to the Mastic Neck and Poospatuck landscape. The dated deed reference is handled as a timeline entry so the public text can remain concise while the references stays visible through the reference icon.
translation_content:
The name is interpreted as possibly related to words meaning measure or to measure. The interpretation connects the placename with land that was measured or laid out for Native use.

Why Place Names Matter

“Place names also record Traditional Knowledge about local resources, the environment or land forms. They can contain information about ecosystems and plants and animals living there.”

— First Nations Education Steering Committee and First Nations Schools Association, BC First Peoples 12 Teacher Resource Guide (2022), Line Master 4-1, page 151

Place-name history should show Native people as active and present, not only as names in old documents.
preservation_content: Qualican preserves the name of a smaller tract within the Unkechaug homeland, showing how named acres, necks, meadows, and reservation lands were recorded inside colonial land documents.
